content.text:
No stale references to the old sentinel remain (only the test name). Done — changes are staged in the working tree, not committed.

## What changed

**`lib/content-type.js:22`** — the parameter regex value group became an alternation: a full quoted-string (group 2) tried first, or the previous lenient token match (group 3) as fallback.

```js
/(?:^|;)\s*([\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+)=(?:("(?:[\t\x20\x21\x23-\x5b\x5d-\x7e\x80-\xff]|\\[\t\x20-\x7e\x80-\xff])*")|([^;]*))/gm
```

The qdtext class excludes `"` (0x22) and `\` (0x5c), so it is disjoint from the quoted-pair branch and the match stays linear — a 200k-char unterminated value parses in ~5ms.

**`lib/content-type.js:155-172`** — when group 2 matched, the DQUOTEs are stripped and quoted-pairs unescaped via the new `quotedPairReg` (skipped entirely when no `\` is present, to keep the common path allocation-free). When group 3 matched but starts with `"`, the value is an unterminated quoted-string and the parameter is dropped — replacing the `'invalid quoted string'` sentinel that `parameters.has()`/`get()` could not distinguish from a real value.

All three reported cases now behave: `name="foo;bar"` → `foo;bar`; `name="a=b;charset=fake"` → one `name` parameter, no phantom `charset`; `name="he said \"hi\""` → `he said "hi"`.

## Tests

- `test/content-type.test.js` — three new unit tests for the cases above; `skips invalid quoted string parameters` updated to expect the unterminated parameter to be dropped (size 2, absent from `toString()`). 14/14 pass.
- `test/internals/reply.test.js:1273` — integration test asserting `reply.send()` appends `charset=utf-8` for `application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"`. 82/82 pass in that file.

I did not run lint (the command needed approval I didn't have), so those two files are unverified against eslint; nothing in them uses unusual syntax for this repo.

## Notes

- Per COMPLEX.md's co-change rule, I opened `lib/reply.js` — it is the consumer of `parameters.has('charset')` at `lib/reply.js:216` and needed no change; the fix is entirely in the parser. No error codes, warnings, or public types changed, so `types/` and `docs/` need no update.
- One edge case beyond the issue: a quoted value containing code points above `\xff` (e.g. non-Latin-1 UTF-8 text) no longer matches the quoted branch and is now dropped rather than kept. That matches `fast-content-type-parse`, whose grammar also stops at obs-text (0x80–0xFF), but it is a behavior change from the old `[^;]*` catch-all — worth a line in the PR description if you want it called out.
